title: C210 — Inline connector reading guide
introduction:
This inline connection is a busy little junction: the assignment tables include speaker circuits, fuel-level signals, convertible-top functions, audio enable, a ground and communication-network circuits. I use the Function column to understand each circuit's job, then the cavity labels to find its address in the drawing. Sharing a housing does not make those circuits interchangeable.

Choose the MALE or FEMALE harness section first. Each has its own face drawing, identification row and Face pins table. As drawn, the male face carries the lower-numbered column on the left and the female face carries it on the right. The columns are vertically staggered, so follow the printed labels rather than treating horizontally adjacent circles as a numbered pair. Use the housing outline as a visual landmark without assigning a release function to its projections.

For each cavity, read Circuit Number, Color, Gauge, Function, Qualifier, Used and Terminal Part Number together. Keep speaker polarity and network high/low labels attached to their named circuits. Repeated cavities can have alternative assignments or entries with different recorded wire and terminal details. Blank qualifiers do not tell you which alternative belongs to a particular car. Compare each harness side's own row rather than assuming its wire color, gauge or terminal must match the other side.

The gray-filled positions can be cross-checked against the blank assignment rows; shading is no electrical test result. This reference does not define physical viewing direction, Size, Used or the gauge convention. It also does not teach connector access, release, probing or repair. Keep literal unavailable terminal entries unchanged and use a matching service procedure before undertaking that work.

The summary Pin Count disagrees with the numbered positions shown in both face drawings. That discrepancy remains unresolved; the summary does not establish additional physical cavities.

edits.why: The harness heading keeps this face tied to its own identification and assignment tables. I navigate by its printed cavity labels and staggered columns; unlabeled housing features provide visual landmarks without establishing how the connector releases.

The following rows belong to the male face. Read each circuit's full function, including polarity or network high/low designation, before comparing alternatives. Repeated entries with blank qualifiers cannot establish the installed equipment configuration or justify a terminal choice.

This drawing reverses the column placement seen in the male drawing. Its own labels and housing outline keep the reference readable without assuming a physical viewing direction or carrying over the other face's left-and-right positions.

The following rows describe the female side. Corresponding circuit identifiers allow comparison, while each side retains its own recorded color, gauge and terminal information. A difference across the harness connection is not, by itself, evidence of an incorrect wire or a fault.

originalAuthorHold: The identification table labels Pin Count as 26, while both supplied face drawings label cavities 1–20. The evidence leaves the meaning of Pin Count unresolved. Clarify whether it counts assignment entries or represents a conflicting physical count before describing the connector's cavity total.

editorialRevision.scope: Complete independent active-agent review of all 75 primary units, four complete pages/two figures and four edits. Original first CLI author covered 59 units/four headings. Complete draft explicitly discloses the count discrepancy and covers all table rows and raw text. Original partial author retained separately; physical count, equipment applicability and literal assignment alternatives remain unresolved for bounded source reading only.
